clue.text: Writer's quarters containing a small bed

indicators.note: one thing containing another holds it inside, so the bed sits between the quarters

parts.note: two quarters of the compass, south and east, taken as single letters
a crib is a baby's cot

explanation.surface: A writer's living quarters with a cramped little bed in them.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass quarters split around the cot: S at the front and E at the back give SCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, originally a professional copyist of documents.

clue.text: Drink and quickly grow bigger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade
second meaning: to increase rapidly, as a ball rolled in snow does

explanation.surface: Drink, and you will soon put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an advocaat cocktail and, as a verb, the way a problem gathers size and momentum.

clue.text: Animal, headless ox, covered by boulder

indicators.note: covered by means the boulder word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a boulder is a large rock

indicators.note: without its head the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the zebu is a humped ox of Asia and Africa

explanation.surface: A beast without its head, buried under a fallen boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: The zebu is a humped ox of India; losing its head means only its first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is the male of the roe deer, so it is an animal.

clue.text: To produce something edible, country needs teachers

parts.note: Brazil is a country in South America
the NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A nation needs teachers in order to grow its food.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the main British teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut is the large oily seed of a South American tree, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Investigate till it's time to leave

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look into something, as a phrasal verb
second meaning: the counter where you pay in a shop
third meaning: the hour a hotel guest must vacate the room

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep digging until it is time to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' reads as 'until' in the surface, but it is the shop counter, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a verb for examining, a noun for a supermarket pay point, and the hotel departure hour.

clue.text: Vandal races man against mule, for a game

parts.note: the Vandals and the Huns were both barbarian tribes that sacked Rome
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races held on the Isle of Man
he is the male pronoun
a mule is a backless slipper

explanation.surface: A hooligan pits a man against a mule in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunt the slipper is a children's party game in which a shoe is passed round a circle behind the players' backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunt the slipper is a traditional parlour game in which one player tries to find a hidden shoe.

clue.text: A hundred and four characters, roughly, in this place-name

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, not in exact order, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the four letters of the word four itself

explanation.surface: Counting roughly how many letters a place-name has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four characters' sounds like a count of letters; it is the word four itself to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is the name of a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, so it is a place-name.

clue.text: Several days' work for widespread, powerful organization

parts.note: October is a month, several days; OCT is its calendar abbreviation
an opus is a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: A few days' labour for a big, influential company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several days' is a loose way of pointing at a month, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is used figuratively for an organization with far-reaching tentacles of influence in many places.

clue.text: Army attacked one island

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
to hit is to attack
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops invade a single island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Right map fliers used wrongly — they landed in Massachusetts
Manoeuvre rope into a coil

indicators.note: putting something into a coil winds it round and changes its shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for winding a rope into a neat coil.
explanation.definitionFit: A military operation is a planned movement of troops, so a manoeuvre in the strategic sense.

clue.text: Heave unfortunate wife out

indicators.note: a person who is out has left, so this letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an unfortunate is a poor soul, a wretch
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A miserable husband heaves a sigh after his wife walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' looks like an adjective but is a noun here: an unfortunate person.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to make the motion of vomiting, which is exactly what retching describes.

clue.text: Being extravagant with colour in gouache, initially

parts.note: blue is a colour
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of gouache

explanation.surface: A painter being lavish with the blue in a gouache picture.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British slang to blue money is to squander it, so blueing means spending lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly, so blueing means squandering lavishly.

clue.text: Proclaim chief piece of baggage missing

indicators.note: the chief piece is the head, the very first letter of the word
missing says that leading letter has gone from the word

parts.note: a baggage is an old word for a shameless woman, a strumpet

explanation.surface: An airline announcement that the most important suitcase has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baggage' looks like luggage; here it is the old insult for a hussy, and losing its S leaves TRUMPET.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly and widely, as a herald blowing a horn would.

clue.text: Find equality in love with a Knight

parts.note: to love something is, mildly, to like it
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A romantic finding that being in love with a knight makes them equals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is not O here, as it so often is in crosswords; it is a verb meaning like.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them and declare them similar or equivalent.

clue.text: Romantic inclination after 21

indicators.note: after says the inclination word goes second, following the cross-referenced word

parts.note: 21 down is a word for a notion, and an idea is a synonym
a ship's list is its lean or tilt

explanation.surface: A dreamer's leaning, prompted by a vague hunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 21 down, INKLING, whose synonym IDEA goes first because the inclination comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic, as a noun, is someone who pursues lofty dreams over reality, which is what an idealist does.

clue.text: Cutter cut round bristle on man's face

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it on both sides

parts.note: to cut prices is to lower them
an awn is the bristle on an ear of barley

indicators.note: the face is the front, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of man

explanation.surface: A barber trimming the bristles on a man's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bristle on man's face' suggests stubble, but it is a cereal bristle plus the man's first letter, inside LOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is a machine that cuts grass, so it is a cutter.

clue.text: In pain? Diagnose disorder

indicators.note: disorder means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A patient in pain asks the doctor to diagnose the disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised describes someone suffering acute physical or mental suffering, which is being in pain.

clue.text: A lot to say, but not much to eat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long word or phrase that is hard to pronounce
second meaning: a small amount of food taken in one bite

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings pull in opposite directions, one large and one small, which is the joke of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tongue-twisting long name and the modest quantity of food filling the mouth once.

clue.text: Finished drink — that's a bit of coincidence

parts.note: something over is finished
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone who has just finished a drink remarks on a coincidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Coincidence here is geometry, two things occupying the same space, not chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is where two things partly coincide, covering the same area or period.

clue.text: Listen to the band in distress

indicators.note: listening means we take the word by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a ring is a band, as round a finger

explanation.surface: Hearing a band play while you are miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a circle of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring is to torment or cause anguish, as in wringing someone's heart, so it means to distress.

clue.text: Line put in, adding colour to clue

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so the line goes into the next word

parts.note: inking is adding colour with ink
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A setter adds a line and some colour to a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clue' looks like a crossword clue; it means a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or suspicion, so a clue in the sense of an indication.

clue.text: Out of true, like a trainee worker

parts.note: as means like, in comparison
L is a learner, from the British learner-driver plate
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A trainee worker whose work is crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at an angle or slanting, so not straight, which is out of true.

clue.text: Fruit juice made into a jelly containing mint perhaps

indicators.note: containing means the jelly word holds the herb inside it

parts.note: a jelly that has firmed has set
mint is an example of a herb, signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: A recipe: fruit juice turned into a jelly with mint in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made into a jelly' is a single verb, SET, split around the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet originally meant a cooling Middle Eastern drink of sweetened fruit juice, a sense still in dictionaries.

clue.text: Indispensable cove laid up, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us to go by what the phrase sounds like spoken

parts.note: a cove is a bay; laid up means sick in bed

explanation.surface: An essential fellow is reported to be laid up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' is also British slang for a fellow, which is the surface's reading; here it is the inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental and essential, the core that cannot be done without.

clue.text: Fruit the family grill as a starter

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them, to pump them for information
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: The family barbecues fruit as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grill' suggests cooking, but it means interrogate; 'as a starter' puts that piece in front of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is the large orange gourd, botanically a fruit since it carries the plant's seeds.

clue.text: Weight-lifter, a sailor, suffering setback

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a setback sends something back the way it came, so the sailor is read backwards

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who lifts weights has a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Atlas was the Titan made to hold up the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas bore the sky on his shoulders, making him the archetypal lifter of a heavy weight.

clue.text: Flower seed Lewis scattered

indicators.note: scattered things are thrown about in no order, so the letters land rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A man called Lewis sowing flower seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a small white alpine plant with woolly bracts, the emblem of the Alps.

clue.text: Kind found in equivalent parts

definitions.note: adjective phrase: describing an actor always given similar roles

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A kind of thing discovered in equal portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past of find, but it is the foundry verb meaning to cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast keeps getting roles of the same sort, so always appears in similar parts.

clue.text: Fellow stiff and cold

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
rigid means stiff, unbending

explanation.surface: A man who is stiff and chilly in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means extremely chilly in temperature, and by extension unfriendly in manner.
